questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A Hydrogen-like atom has atomic number $Z$. Photons emitted in the electronic transitions from level $n = 4$ to level $n = 3$ in these atoms are used to perform photoelectric effect experiment on a target metal. The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons generated is $1 . 95eV$. If the photoelectric threshold wavelength for the target metal is $310nm$, the value of $Z$ is _____.

[Given $hc = 1240eV - nm$ and $Rhc = 13 . 6eV$, where $R$ is the Rydberg constant, $h$ is the Planck’s constant and $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum]
questions.solution:
From Einstein's photoelectric effect, we can write

$E = K{E}_{max} + ϕ ⇒ E = K{E}_{max} + \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

$⇒ ∆ {E}_{4to3} = 1 . 95eV + \dfrac{1240}{310}eV ⇒ ∆ {E}_{4to3} = 5 . 95eV$

Now, as we know for Hydrogen like atoms, we can write $∆ E = 13 . 6{Z}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{{\left({n}_{1}\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\left({n}_{2}\right)}^{2}}\right)$

Therefore,$⇒ 13 . 6{Z}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{{3}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{4}^{2}}\right) = 5 . 95$

$⇒ 13 . 6{Z}^{2}\dfrac{7}{9 \times 16} = 5 . 95$

$⇒ {Z}^{2} = \dfrac{5 . 95 \times 9 \times 16}{13 . 6 \times 7} = 9$

$⇒ Z = 3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When light of a given wavelength is incident on a metallic surface, the minimum potential needed to stop the emitted photoelectrons is $6 . 0V$. This potential drops to $0 . 6V$ if another source with wavelength four times that of the first one and intensity half of the first one is used. What are the wavelength of the first source and the work function of the metal, respectively? [Take$\dfrac{hc}{e} = 1 . 24 \times {10}^{- 6}J{mC}^{- 1}$ .]
questions.solution:
According to the Einstein's equation of photoelectric effect for the first case,

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - ϕ = 6eV ⋯ ( i )$

And for the second case,

$\dfrac{hc}{4\lambda} - ϕ = 0 . 6eV$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{3hc}{4\lambda} = 5 . 4eV$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{3hc}{4 \times 5 . 4eV} = \dfrac{3 \times 1 . 24 \times {10}^{- 6}}{4 \times 5 . 4}$

$⇒ \lambda = 1 . 72 \times {10}^{- 7}m$

$⇒$ from equation $\left(i\right)$

$\dfrac{hc}{1 . 72 \times {10}^{- 7}} \times \dfrac{1}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}} - ϕ = 6eV$

$\dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 25}}{2 . 75 \times {10}^{- 26}} - ϕ = 6$

$⇒ ϕ = \left(7 . 27 - 6\right) ≅ 1 . 2eV$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a photoemission experiment, the maximum kinetic energies of photoelectrons from metals $P, Q$ and $R$ are ${E}_{P}, {E}_{Q}$ and ${E}_{R}$, respectively, and they are related by ${E}_{P} = 2{E}_{Q} = 2{E}_{R}$. In this experiment, the same source of monochromatic light is used for metals $P$ and $Q$ while a different source of monochromatic light is used for the metal $R$. The work functions for metals $P, Q$ and $R$ are $4 . 0eV, 4 . 5eV$ and $5 . 5eV$, respectively. The energy of the incident photon used for metal $R$, in $eV$ is ___.
questions.solution:
Let the maximum kinetic energies of photoelectrons be${E}_{P} = 2{E}_{Q} = 2{E}_{R} = 2E$.

The energy of incident photon on metal $P\text{and}Q$ be $U$ and for $R$ be $U '$.

Photoelectric equation, ${E}_{ph} = ϕ + K{E}_{max}$

Now, using it for the three cases,

$U = 4 + 2E . . . \left(1\right)U = 4 . 5 + E . . . \left(2\right)U ' = 5 . 5 + E . . . \left(3\right)

From \left(1\right) \text{and}\left(2\right)$, $E = 0 . 5eV$

From $\left(3\right)$, energy of the incident photon for metal $R$,

$U ' = 5 . 5 + 0 . 5 = 6eV$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A perfectly reflecting mirror of mass $M$ mounted on a spring constitutes a spring-mass system of angular frequency $Ω$ such that $\dfrac{4\piMΩ}{h} = {10}^{24}{m}^{- 2}$ with $h$ as Planck's constant. $N$ photons of wavelength $\lambda = 8\pi \times {10}^{- 6}m$ strike the mirror simultaneously at normal incidence such that the mirror gets displaced by $1\mum .$ If the value of $N$ is $x \times {10}^{12},$ then the value of $x$ is________.
[Consider the spring as massless]
questions.solution:
Total Momentum transferred on mirror $= \dfrac{2Nh}{\lambda}$ (for perfect reflection)
In an $SHM$
${V}_{max} = A . Ω$
Where $A =$ amplitude and $Ω =$ angular frequency
$⇒ \dfrac{2Nh}{\lambda} = M{V}_{\left(meanposition\right)}$
$\begin{cases}{V}_{\left(meanposition\right)} = ΩA & \left(whereA = 1\mum\right)\end{cases}$
$⇒ \begin{cases}\dfrac{2Nh}{\lambda} = MΩA & \left(where\lambda = 8\pi \times {10}^{- 6}\right)\end{cases}$
$∴ N = \dfrac{\lambdaMΩA}{2h}$
$⇒ N = \dfrac{MΩ\left({10}^{- 6}\right)\lambda}{2h} = \dfrac{MΩ8\pi \times {10}^{- 6} \times {10}^{- 6}}{2h}$
$N = \dfrac{4\piMΩ}{h} \times {10}^{- 12}$
$= {10}^{24} \times {10}^{- 12}$
$N = 1 \times {10}^{12}$
$x = 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a photoelectric experiment, a parallel beam of monochromatic light with the power of $200\text{W}$ is incident on a perfectly absorbing cathode of work function $6.25eV$. The frequency of light is just above the threshold frequency so that the photoelectrons are emitted with negligible kinetic energy. Assume that the photoelectron emission efficiency is 100%. A potential difference of $500\text{V}$ is applied between the cathode and the anode. All the emitted electrons are incident normally on the anode and are absorbed. The anode experiences a force $F = n \times {10}^{- 4}N$ due to the impact of the electrons. The value of $n$ is __________. Mass of the electron ${m}_{e} = 9 \times {10}^{- 31}kgand1.0eV = 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}J$.
questions.solution:
Power $= Nhν$
$N =$ number of photons per second
Since $KE = 0, hν = ϕ$
$200 = N\left[6.25 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}Joule\right]$
$N = \dfrac{200}{6.25 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}}$
As photon is just above threshold frequency $K{E}_{max}$ is zero and they are accelerated by potential difference of $500V$
$K{E}_{f} = q∆V$
$\dfrac{{P}^{2}}{2m} = q∆V ⇒ P = \sqrt{2mq∆V}$
Since efficiency is 100%, number of electrons emitted is equal to number of photons falling per second as electrons are completely absorbed, force exerted $nmv$
$= \dfrac{200}{6.25 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}} \times \sqrt{2\left(9 \times {10}^{- 31}\right) \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 500}$
$= \dfrac{3 \times 200 \times {10}^{- 25} \times \sqrt{1600}}{6.25 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}} = \dfrac{2 \times 40}{6.25 \times 1.6} \times {10}^{- 4} \times 3 = 24\times {10}^{- 4}$
$n = 24$

questions.q: A photoelectric material having work-function ${ϕ}_{0}$ is illuminated with a light of wavelength $\lambda\left(\lambda < \dfrac{hc}{{ϕ}_{0}}\right)$. The fastest photoelectron has a de Broglie wavelength ${\lambda}_{d}$. A change in wavelength of the incident light by $\Delta\lambda$ results in a change $\Delta{\lambda}_{d}$ in ${\lambda}_{d}$. The ratio $\dfrac{\Delta{\lambda}_{d}}{\Delta\lambda}$ is proportional to
questions.solution:
According to the equation of photoelectric effect,

$K{E}_{max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - {ϕ}_{0}$

Kinetic energy in terms of momentum is given as $KE = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}$

$\dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - {ϕ}_{0}$

$\dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{h}{{\lambda}_{d}}\right)}^{2}}{2m} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - {ϕ}_{0}$

Assuming small changes, differentiating both sides,

$\dfrac{{h}^{2}}{2m}\left(- \dfrac{2d{\lambda}_{d}}{{\lambda}_{d}^{3}}\right) = - \dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}^{2}}d\lambda$

$\dfrac{d{\lambda}_{d}}{d\lambda} ∝ \dfrac{{\lambda}_{d}^{3}}{{\lambda}^{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light of wavelength ${\lambda}_{ph}$ falls on a cathode plate inside a vacuum tube as shown in the figure. The work function of the cathode surface is $ϕ$ and the anode is a wire mesh of conducting material kept at a distance d from the cathode. A potential difference V is maintained between the electrodes. If the minimum de Broglie wavelength of the electrons passing through the anode is ${\lambda}_{e},$ which of the following statement(s) is(are) true ?
options: For large potential difference $\left(\text{V} ≫ \dfrac{ϕ}{\text{e}}\right) , {λ}_{\text{e}}$ is approximately halved if V is made four times
${λ}_{\text{e}}$ increases at the same rate as ${λ}_{\text{ph}} for {λ}_{\text{ph}} < \dfrac{\text{hc}}{ϕ}$
${λ}_{ⅇ}$ is approximately halved, if d is doubled
questions.solution:
${K}_{max} = \dfrac{hc}{{λ}_{Ph}} - ϕ$
Kinetic energy of ${e}^{-}$ reaching the anode will be
$K = \dfrac{hc}{{λ}_{Ph}} - ϕ + eV$
Now ${λ}_{e} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m\left(\dfrac{hc}{{λ}_{Ph}} - ϕ + eV\right)}}$
If $eV ≫ ϕ$
${λ}_{e} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m\left(\dfrac{hc}{{λ}_{Ph}} + eV\right)}}$
If ${V}_{f} = 4{V}_{i}$
${\left({λ}_{e}\right)}_{f} ≃ \dfrac{{\left({λ}_{e}\right)}_{i}}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In a historical experiment to determine Planck's constant, a metal surface was irradiated with light of different wavelengths. The emitted photoelectron energies were measured by applying a stopping potential. The relevant data for the wavelength $( \lambda )$ of incident light and the corresponding stopping potential $\left({V}_{0}\right)$ are given below:
$\lambda\left(\mum\right) ${V}_{0}$\left(Volt\right)$
0.3 2.0
0.4 1.0
0.5 0.4

Given that $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}ande = 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}C,$ Planck's constant (in units of J s) found from such an experiment is :
questions.solution:
$K{E}_{max} = \dfrac{hC}{\lambda} - ϕ$

$e\left({V}_{0}\right) = \dfrac{hC}{\lambda} - ϕ$
$1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 2 = \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{3000 \times {10}^{- 10}} - ϕ$ .....(i)
$1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 1 = \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{4000 \times {10}^{- 10}} - ϕ$ .......(ii)
From (ii) $ϕ = \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{4000 \times {10}^{- 10}} - 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}$

Using value of $ϕ$ in equation (i), we get
$1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 2 = \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{3000 \times {10}^{- 10}} - \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{4000 \times {10}^{- 10}} + 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}$
$1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} = \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{{10}^{- 7}}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{{10}^{- 7}}\left[\dfrac{4 - 3}{12}\right]$
$1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} = \dfrac{h \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{{10}^{- 7}} \times \dfrac{1}{12}$
$1.6 \times 4 \times \dfrac{{10}^{- 19} \times {10}^{- 7}}{{10}^{8}} = h$
$6.4 \times {10}^{- 34}Js = h$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron in an excited state of $L{i}^{2 +}$ ion has angular momentum $\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$ . The de Broglie wavelength of the electron in this state is $p\pi{\alpha}_{0}$ (where ${a}_{0}$ is the Bohr radius). The value of $p$ is
questions.solution:
From Bohr's law
$mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi} = \dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$ (from eqes.)
$⇒ n = 3$
And momentum $= mv = \dfrac{3h}{2\pir}$
Now, radius of ${n}^{th}$ shell, $r = \left(\dfrac{{n}^{2}}{z}\right){a}_{0}$
$⇒ r = \dfrac{{\left(3\right)}^{2}}{3} . {a}_{0} \left[∵ {Z}_{Li} = 3\right]$
$⇒ r = 3{a}_{0}$
From De Broglie law
$wavelength = \dfrac{h}{Momentum}$
$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv} = \dfrac{h}{\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}r}$
$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{2\pir}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} \times 3{a}_{0}$
$\lambda = 2\pi{a}_{0} = p\pi{a}_{0}$
$⇒ P = 2$

questions.q: Consider a hydrogen atom with its electron in the ${n}^{th}$ orbital. An electromagnetic radiation of wavelength 90 nm is used to ionize the atom. If the kinetic energy of the ejected electron is 10.4 eV, then the value of n is $\left(hc = 1242eVnm\right)$
questions.solution:
${E}_{Ph} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{1242}{90} = 13.8eV$
${E}_{Ph} = ∆ E + ( K . E . )$
$13.8 = ∆ E + 10.4$
$∆ E = 3.4eV$
So electron initially was in $n = 2$

& $\text{$ or $} \quad$n= $\frac{1.5 \times 10^{-2}}{9 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-10}}=$1.04 $\times$10^7

questions.q: An $\alpha$-particle and a proton are accelerated from rest by a potential difference of $100 \mathrm{~V}$. After this, their de Broglie wavelengths are $\lambda_\alpha$ and $\lambda_p$ respectively. The ratio $\frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha}$, to the nearest integer, is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
\lambda$& =$\frac{h}{P}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 q q V m}} \text{$ or $} \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{q m}}$\\
$\frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha}$& =$\sqrt{\frac{q_\alpha}{q_p} \cdot \frac{m_{\propto}}{m_p}}=\sqrt{\frac{(2)(4)}{(1)(1)}}=$2.828
\end{aligned}$ The nearest integer is 3 .\therefore$ answer is 3 .

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electrons with de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ fall on the target in an X-ray tube. The cut-off wavelength of the emitted X-rays is
options:
$\lambda_0=\frac{2 m c \lambda^2}{h}$

$\lambda_0=\frac{2 h}{m c}$

$\lambda_0=\frac{2 m^2 c^2 \lambda^3}{h^2}$

$\lambda_0=\lambda$
questions.solution:
Momentum of striking electrons, $p=\frac{h}{\lambda}$
$\therefore$ Kinetic energy of striking electrons, $K=\frac{p^2}{2 m}=\frac{h^2}{2 m \lambda^2}$
This is also, maximum energy of $X$-ray photons.
Therefore, $\quad \frac{h c}{\lambda_0}=\frac{h^2}{2 m \lambda^2}$ or $\lambda_0=\frac{2 m \lambda^2 c}{h}$
$\therefore$ Correct option is (a).
